utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls Zehra Turjacanin. Your Honour, I see Mr. Dieckmann is standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Dieckmann.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a very short matters for the record. Regarding exhibit 2D16, this document was released under the number 2D01-0707. This is the wrong number, and just for the record the correct number for this document would be 2D03-0003. That's all. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration. Please make the declaration. Please read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is your name? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure if I'm the only person, but I heard French translation through my headset, and I'm not sure the witness is able to hear. Is there a technical problem?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you hear me? Ms. Turjacanin, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I am Zehra Turjacanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When were you born?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At Turjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where is that located? What country is that located in?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It is Opsinobica [as interpreted] in the municipality of Visegrad in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could kindly ask the usher to please show the witness a pseudonym sheet. The witness is testifying in open session but will refer to someone who has protective measures. Ms. Turjacanin, I would ask you to look at the piece of paper the usher is now showing you. It contains the name of a person. Without saying the name of this person, do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I know this person. VG-38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This person has protective measures and is referred to as VG-32. How did you know this person prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It's the husband of my best friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would now tender that pseudonym sheet as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number P131, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Turjacanin, it will eventually be placed before you as a reminder and I would ask at any time during your testimony if you need to refer to this person that you refer to them by their pseudonym VG-32. My next question to you is did you attend secondary school?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, drawing your attention to the spring of 1992, where were you living at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At Nabikot [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember the address?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: 19 Bilovanovic [phoen] number 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My apologies for interrupting but it is a wrong number on this pseudonym sheet. It has to be VG-32, not 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry if there's a mistake. If I could ask that it be amended to reflect VG-32. I apologise if there is a typographical error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let that be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The house that you've just mentioned, did it have a new section as well as an older section?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many floors were in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: There were three floors if you count the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The top floor, did it have a balcony?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, there was one.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When standing on the balcony of your house in Bikavac, what could you see before you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I could see people from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see the new bridge in the town?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the month of June 1992, did you look out over the -- that area from the balcony after night had fallen?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How often?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Practically all evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you see and hear during the month of June from your balcony in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Every evening I could see Elevir Cuk [as interpreted] who was arriving on the bridge, and at a given moment when a car came on the bridge, the lights went off, and that moment Elevir Cuk and men -- we could hear screams and shots and finally the noise of bodies falling in the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the month of June can you estimate how many nights that you were up in the balcony that you made such observations?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Every evening. We couldn't sleep. Every evening I was on my balcony and I was looking what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to the war did you know a person by the name of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At school. We knew each other at school. We were schoolmates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you and him go to the same school?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you in the same classes as him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you in the same year as him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what year you were in at the time you were in the same school as Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was in first year and I was in the fourth year.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is this in the secondary school?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have a sibling that also attended that school? Did you have a brother or sister who also attended that school?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it a brother or a sister?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was a brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Dzevad Turjacanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know what year he was born?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know whether Dzevad Turjacanin also knew Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did your brother know Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Because they were in the same class at school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did your brother ever speak about who he shared his classroom table with?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who did he share his classroom table with?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: With Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, during the course of a school day, were there breaks between classes?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Every 45 minutes there was a change of class.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many breaks in total would there be in any given school day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would students do during these breaks?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Eat a sandwich, drink something, smoke a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Students who used to smoke during the breaks, where would they smoke?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you yourself smoke while you were at the school?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever see Milan Lukic smoking while you were smoking during class breaks?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you estimate for us how many times per week or per month you would have seen Milan Lukic smoking a cigarette while you were smoking a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I could say perhaps once -- once a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time in June of 1992 when a group of armed men arrived in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember the exact date of when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to summarise what happened when these men arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At a given moment they came from everywhere, and they started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do when this started?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Since they were shooting from everywhere, we lay down on the floor, on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this point in time was your brother Dzevad still in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During June of 1992, was your brother Dzevad still in Visegrad, in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where precisely was he?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was at Nova Lamazon [as interpreted] on the ground floor in the block.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So are you saying that he was in the house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us precisely where in the house he was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he hiding in any way?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please explain?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: With the blocks of concrete we had barricaded the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When he was hiding in this -- in this manner, was he able to get out of where he was hiding without assistance?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there anyone else hiding with him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time in June of 1992 that you saw Milan Lukic in the Bikavac area?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I was at my neighbour's.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is the name of your neighbour?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Dzemila Kahriman.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when you say your neighbour, how far was Dzemila Kahriman's house from your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: About a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What were you doing at her house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: We were having coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who else was present?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: A few other neighbours, ladies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What time of the day was this?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At the end of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it still light out?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there still sunlight out?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when someone came and spoke with yourself and the other women having coffee?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was Milan Lukic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe the circumstances around Milan Lukic speaking with yourself and the other women?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He appeared behind the house. He saluted us, greeted us politely. He said, "I have come to see how you're faring, and don't be worried. Don't be worried. I will protect you."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you offer him coffee?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did one of the women offer him coffee?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: At this time I mean I've been -- you know I understand the foundational nature of sometimes getting a witness into testimony, but it is done in a leading manner with always placing a fact in the question that sort of leads the witness. I believe that the nature of the questioning is leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe I've asked any leading questions. Leading questions suggest an answer to a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, did one of the women offer him coffee. That's suggesting coffee and yes as the answer. So that would be leading but I don't know if that's a matter of any controversy.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, the reason being is oftentimes the direct exam is also to test the recollection of the witness. That's why the questions are left open. If the Prosecution always fills in the detail which it cues the witness and therefore it does not test the independent recollection of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Therefore, Mr. Groome, we will apply the rule very strictly, and please avoid any leading questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic offered anything by anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The lady offered coffee to Milan Lukic, and he refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How was he dressed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he armed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How far away were you from him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: About a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you have a clear view of his face?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you recognise him at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who did you recognise him to be?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did it take you to recognise him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you working in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Visegrad. In Alhos, Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what kind of enterprise was that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was women's clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was your position there? What was your work there?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: A seamstress.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you get back and forth from work?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: On foot. I walked.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever see Milan Lukic at the place where you worked?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: In June, an afternoon in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was it before or after the time you saw him when you were having coffee?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was after the coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know why he came to the factory?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He came to get his neighbour lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall her name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall her ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: She was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What time of the day was this?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Around 1800. 6.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe the lighting witness in the factory at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was a very good lighting because you need that to be able to sew.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe that for us?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was in a black suit with black coat also.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was the woman that he was looking for present in the factory?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did he remain there?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was there a time in June that one of your sisters described a conversation that she had with someone?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. She came from the town, and she told us that she had seen Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What's the name of this sister?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Dzehva.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When did she tell you that she had this conversation with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: When she came at home she said that she had seen Milan Lukic and she had spoken to him. They had spoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us what month this occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did she tell you where precisely they had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: At the old bridge of the Drina, on the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did she tell you what was said during the course of the conversation?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what you recall about what she told you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please tell us now.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He asked him where is your brother Dzevad, he asked from her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did she say that he asked for your brother by his name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I now want to draw your attention to the latter part of June 1992 to the Bikavac area of Visegrad. Can I ask you to describe for us what was the atmosphere like during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was a very strange atmosphere. Things were always happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "things," could I ask you to be more specific. What types of things were always happening?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Pressure being exerted. Well, we were anticipating or expecting that things were going to happen. There was fear. It was just -- just a very strange atmosphere and there was a lot of fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you a person by the name of Enver Subasic?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is he alive today?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what you know about his death?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, a group of men were brought by Milan Lukic and they burnt everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you -- did you personally witness his death?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to tell us where you were when you witnessed his death?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I was on a path about ten metres away from my house, and the men brought Mr. Subasic, and a bit later they set the fire and people were running in all directions, and the men were shouting at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You are referring to a fire. Can you be specific about what exactly you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've referred to a fire. Let me ask you, you've said that you personally witnessed his death. How did Enver Subasic die?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, when you douse someone with fire and set fire --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, the interpreter --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- when you douse someone with gas and you set fire to him, then of course he burns.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he the only person who died in that way that day that you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who else?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: An elderly man, Deda Musevic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you also personally witness his death?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. He burned at the same time as Enver Subasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us precisely where these two men were burned?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Negrad [phoen]. In town.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where is that in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Two hundred and fifty metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now call your attention to the very end of June and a very significant event occurred. Can I ask you to tell us as best you recall the date that this event occurred.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The 27th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember what day of the week it was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall if there was a holiday that day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. It was a Saturday and a holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What holiday was it?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It's an Orthodox holiday. It's called Vidovdan, St. Vitus.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not your Serb neighbours celebrated on this day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, they always did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did they celebrate on this particular Vidovdan day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: That I couldn't really say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know whether they remained in the Bikavac area or whether they left the Bikavac area?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what did they do?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: They left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know where they went to?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: They went into the mountains that were between Visegrad and Sarajevo, Umero [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the weather like at that day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: There was some rain, but there was also sunshine occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you spend the day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us all of the people who were with you in your home that day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: On that day in my home I was with my mother Djulka, my two sisters, two children of my sister, my sister-in-law and her son, as well as another lady with her son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to make sure that the record records the names of the family members you were with, so could I ask you to tell us the name of your mother.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: My mother's name [Realtime transcript read in error "neighbouring"] was Djulka. Djulka.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned your sisters. Can I ask you to identify them each individually. What was the name of your first sister?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: My older sister was called Dzehva, and my younger sister's name was Aida.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I suppose she said my mother's name is Djulka, not neighbouring.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that is what she said. I'd ask the record be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your sister Dzehva, was she married?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, she was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was her married name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Tufekcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what were her children's names?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't quite grasp the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What were the names of her children?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Their names were Elma and Esad.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And could you please tell us the age of the children in 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Elma was six years old and the little boy was about a year and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, when the witness came to The Hague she brought a picture of her sister and one of her children. It is not on the 65 ter list. We did disclose this it yesterday evening. I wonder whether I'd be permitted to show the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask ERN 04249120 be called up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to look in front of you. Can you see a -- [French on English channel] on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who is depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I see my sister, her little daughter Elma, and her husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number P132, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned that your sister-in-law was present. Can I ask you to please give us her full name.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Sada Turjacanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did she have children?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. She had a son.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: His name was Selmir.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how old was he?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Seven years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You also mentioned another person. Was there another person present in your house that day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us who that person was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember her name, but it was another lady, a neighbour, a neighbour of Milan Lukic, and she was there with her daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where precisely was this -- this woman from? The name the area, if you know.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The name is Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know the name of her daughter?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was her age, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Approximately 16 or 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned your sister Aida. Did Aida have a disability?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to simply briefly tell us what was the nature of Aida's disability?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, she had a slight disability, mental disability.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How would you describe your relationship with Aida?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I was her big sister, and I tried to do my best to always take care of her and take care of her disability.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The afternoon of this day what were these people doing in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: They were sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you leave the house at all this day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever leave your house this day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I went across the street to visit my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the name of this neighbour?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Sena Subasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when a colleague of yours from work visited you that day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the name of this person?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Milan Lucic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was this person's -- what was this person's ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you have an opinion about this man's character?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He is a good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he have a conversation with you this day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we had a talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what he said to you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did he say?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He said, "What are you waiting for? Why haven't you left yet, because surely bad things are going to happen."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe his emotional state during this conversation?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we possibly get the witness to move a little bit closer to her microphone so that we could hear her better?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe his emotional state during this conversation?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was very emotional and extremely sad. He was even crying.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did he stay?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Not very long.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left Sena's house to return to your own home?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you remember what time of the day that was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do upon your return home?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I went out onto the balcony to smoke a cigarette.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While you were smoking that cigarette did anything unusual occur?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I could hear a lot of noise and music.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The music, are you able to remember anything about the type of music that you heard?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. It was the Serbian nationalist music.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you characterise the volume at which that music was being played?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was very loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was the music coming from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: From loudspeakers in the cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After hearing the music what happened?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, after we heard the music, we heard people knocking on the doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: So they knocked on the door. They asked us to come out of the house, and so we came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did all of the people that you've listed for us a few minutes ago, did all of those people come out of the house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. We all came out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was your brother Dzevad at this point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was he hiding in the place that you've described for us earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was anyone else hiding there with him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. My cousin was hiding with him also.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what you saw when you came out of your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would you please do that.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: So we all went out of the house, and people came out of other houses as well. We were -- so we were all together in front of the house. There were some men and soldiers as well, and then the men organised a convoy to take us to Bajina Basta.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say the men organised a convoy to take you to Bajina Basta, can you please tell us precisely what, if anything, was said to you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: They simply said, "We are going to set up a convoy to take you to Bajina Basta."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you came out of your house did you see any buses or other vehicles that could have been used in a convoy?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No. There was nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned soldiers. Can I ask you to describe with as much specificity as you're able what you recall about the soldiers that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: One of the soldiers was Milan Lukic himself, and I remember a second man, his cousin, and his uncle whose name is also Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall this person -- or did you know the second person you're referring to prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him. He used to be a police officer in the town.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It was his cousin or his uncle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to recall the first name of that person, or did you know the first name of that person?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No. I no longer can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe that person's physical appearance?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. He was fairly strong, fairly tall, about 50 years of age.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where precisely did you see Milan Lukic for the first time after you left your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: On the path that separated two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where in relation to the front of your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was pretty much between two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person that you're describing as a cousin or uncle of Milan Lukic, where was he the first time you saw him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was coming down the stairs of my old house with another man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The person that you're describing as the uncle or cousin, do you recall how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe what you remember about how he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was wearing a military uniform, the same type that was worn by all the members of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall whether or not he was armed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What do you remember about that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: In fact, all the men who were on site were -- or had rifles on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the occupants of your house left your house?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter didn't catch the last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your answer, Witness. The interpreter didn't hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We followed that man. We followed that man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "that man," can I ask you to be precise about which man you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, in fact, the men in the plural. I'm sorry. We followed the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did these men lead you to?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: About 100 metres away from my house to another house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the family or the person who owned this house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the name of the family that owned this house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Aljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the name of the head of the household?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Meho Aljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived in front of the Meho Aljic house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: We all went into the house of Meho Aljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recall what you were wearing that day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe what you were wearing, including any jewellery.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I was wearing sneakers, pants, a red T-shirt, a jacket, and I had a small gold chain on my neck.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did anything happen to that small gold chain?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I was the last one to enter the house, and at that moment as I was entering, Milan Lukic himself pulled the gold chain out from under my red T-shirt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what you saw when you first entered the house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, there were lots of people in the house. They were all sitting against the walls in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for the Chamber what the inside of the house looked like? Can you describe the type of room and what you remember about the inside of the house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. It was a fairly large room, rather like a living-room, and next to it was a kitchen. So the -- both rooms, in fact, were connected. They weren't separated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to compare the size of the -- the inside of that house with perhaps, let's say, this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No, I couldn't really.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there other rooms off -- off of the room that you were in?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. There were two other doors in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you have any belief as to whether there were people in these adjoining rooms?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Perhaps, but I didn't check.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe what the front door of this house looked like?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: We didn't actually walk into the house by the front door. We walked in using a door that was on the terrace, a balcony door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe that door for us?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, so it was a large glass door next to the windows that were also in glass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The windows that you're referring to, how close were they to the edge of the door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, they were all together. It was a whole. They were connected to one another, the windows and the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go once you were inside that room?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I stayed close to the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Aida?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: She was right next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was your mother?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: She went and sat down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was your sister Dzehva?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The same thing, she went to sit down somewhere in the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And her children?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: They were with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was your sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And her children?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Her son was with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the woman from Rujiste and her daughter also in the house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to describe what you remember about the other people that you observed in the house? Can you tell us whether they were men or women, their approximate ages? Can you tell us all that you remember about the other people that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: In that house there were mainly young mothers with their small children. There were also a few elderly people, two or three elderly men, also a few elderly women, but unfortunately there were many children in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What would you say was the age of the youngest child you saw in the house that evening?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The son of Suhra, a young mother, her son was not more than a year old.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What's your best recollection as to the time of day that this occurred?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It was approximately 8.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the atmosphere like in that room?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened in that room that night?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The men that I mentioned, first of all they threw rocks at the house to break the -- the windows, and then they threw in some grenades, and then they shot at the walls and the people inside and after that set fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned some grenades. Were you injured in any way when this happened?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. My left leg was injured in several places.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You testified that a fire was set. Can I ask you to describe for us in as much detail as you recall how that happened?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, today I can't remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just if you'd tell us what you do recall today.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, after throwing the rocks and the grenades and shooting at us a fire broke out, and it just happened way too quickly, so quickly. That's really all I can say at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What portion of the house was the fire in?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was the room in which we were, the living-room and the dining-room or kitchen, however you would like to call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you characterise how quickly the fire spread in that room?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. The fire spread extremely quickly, very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did people in the room do?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The people inside were burning alive. They were wailing, screaming. It's just not describable what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did their clothes catch fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, with all the fire and smoke I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did your clothes catch fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Aida at this time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, she was still next to me. In fact, I held her close to me, close to my stomach.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: When I started to -- to really burn and it was unbearable, I remembered where the door was, the door through which I came in, and I tried to escape through that door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to escape through that door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I was surprised when I reached the door. I wanted to -- to go through the door and take my sister with me, but we weren't able to because there was an obstruction, but I did manage to get out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to take your sister with you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No, no, not at all. She stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you got outside of that house were you able to see what it was that was obstructing the door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was it?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, there was another door leaning against the door. It was a metal garage door that was leaning against the door and therefore blocking it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How was it that you were able to get past this garage door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, there was a space of approximately 65 centimetres, and that's what enabled me to get through.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you got outside of the house did you see anyone?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw the men who had caused the fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where precisely were they?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: About 100 metres away. They were lying on the grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you see what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. They were lying on the grass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did they see you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, they saw me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of them say anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, they all shouted at me at the same time. They said, "Stop. Stop."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you stop?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I ran, and as I was doing so I shook off my clothes that were burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where were you running to?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I reason away from the house towards another house, towards Megdan in neighbourhood where the Serbian population was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, Ms. Turjacanin, I'm going to ask you to look at the computer terminal in front you and I want to show you Prosecution Exhibit P54. It is a computer programme that contains 360-degree photos. Could I ask you to look at the computer in front of you and do you see an image on the computer in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No. I don't yet have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the path. I do recognise this. I recognise my garage, and I recognise the stairway of my old house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: And I see part of the wall of my new house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Turjacanin, if I could ask you some specific questions about what we're looking at to maybe assist the Chamber. On the right side of the photograph there is small structure with brown doors. Do you know what this structure is? Did you hear my question?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was my garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Beyond that, also on the right side of the picture, there is a set of concrete steps. Do you recognise those steps?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. That is the staircase of my house, of the house that I used to live in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: There is a house on the left of the screen. Do you recognise that house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who owned that house, if you know?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Nedzib Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The path that we can see in front of us, is this the path that you have testified about that you were on after you came out of your house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to pan to the left. If we could stop there. Now, we can still see the Sadikovic house that you've identified for us, and we can also see another path. Can you describe this path for us?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: This path is the path that leads to the house of Meho Aljic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is this the path where the men led you that night?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. That's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to take us to the back of this house. Okay. Do you recognise what we're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We can see a house in the -- in this picture. Can you tell us whose house that is?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Still the house of Nedzib Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to pan to the left. Please stop there. Can you please describe what we're looking at now in the image?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, you can see some stones and the foundations of a house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was the Meho Aljic house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: On the foundations that you still see here on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to pan to the left. Please stop there. Is there anything in particular about this house that you -- you wish to identify to us?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is it that you wish to identify?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The garage door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that we zoom into that garage door. Is this door similar to the door that was blocking the doorway on the night of the fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you escape? When you described your escape that night, how did you get past these -- or the garage door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I was able to slip through the -- the edge. There was a small opening of about 60 centimetres, and I was able to slip through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: On the image we are now looking at there seems to be an opening at the top of the door. Is that similar to the opening that you escaped through?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome. Reformulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you compare what we're looking at here in terms of what you recall from that night?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: They are exactly identical in terms of colour, exactly identical to the door by which I passed, and I went through an opening that is exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's time for the break. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could ask one more question on this and then I'll be finished with this part of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to pan to the left a little bit more. That's good.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We are now looking at a grassy area on the other side of the path. Is this relevant to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I saw the men lying on the grass when I came out of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the only question I wanted to ask about this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will adjourn, and we'll leave the courtroom after the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will just hear, I believe, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the court assistant had asked me if we could do this after the witness, and I would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm allowing you to do it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, here's the issue, Your Honour. In this case we received disclosures with regards to images that were going to be used and so we've set to working because according to the disclosure sheet filed by the Prosecution last night the still image from 65 ter 0175 showing the garage door through which VG-114 escaped. So by implication of how it was typed it was the actual garage door. I can't tell from the testimony whether it was by her description other than her creating the metaphor. But in looking at the EDS system, Your Honour, and putting in just the simple name of this witness, we made a disturbing discovery that simply is there is an interview notes from the OTP for an interview conducted by Dermot Groome, Yves Roy (redacted) on the 15th and 16th of December, 2000 in relation to over two days and six hours of interview time. For whatever reason the OTP's interview notes are in the system. We've received no statement related -- or any discovery related to these interviews by the OTP. Clearly just from the notations related to the witness's identification of Mitar Vasiljevic, his involvement in the evening of Bikavac fire as well as many other things, and this is clearly exculpatory Rule 68 material and the fact of the matter is, Your Honour, is I was going to be requesting a formal deposition before cross given the nature of the failure to disclose because all I can say, Your Honour, is at this point, I can't -- I can't rule out a wilful failure to disclose relevant discovery to the Defence of Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: As the Court heard me say several weeks ago. The initial contact that we had had with this witness was the process of speaking with her for a few minutes and then her retreating to regain her composure. All of the notes that were taken during that interview or that discussion with her have been disclosed. There is no statement. No statement was taken. She was unable to give any type of formal statement at that time. That's been clearly explained. These notes have been disclosed to the Defence. There are two pages of notes. There is nothing else other to disclose other than the videotaped statements that this witness gave shortly afterwards and they also have been disclosed, so disclosure has been complete in this case. There is nothing else that needs to be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So your position then is that the interview of which Mr. Alarid speaks and which he said took place on the 15th and 16th December, 2000, that that has been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's four pages of notes and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It doesn't matter. He says it has been disclosed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It has not been disclosed. I would ask them to find in the disclosures where this came through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not going to hold up the proceedings now. It's at matter that can take up again --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Van Hooydonk is getting that information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll -- if the usher wouldn't mind, Mr. Alarid can have my copies of those notes if he's unable to find --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No. I got several copies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So you do have copies?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We printed them just this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's not the point, Mr. Groome. He's saying that he only received it this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, not from them. We were searching the electronic discovery system, Your Honour. We were basically just fishing for things and references involving this witness's name and what amounted to is comes out what appears to be internal notes from the district -- or from the Office of the Prosecutor four pages of notes related to interviews related to the Mitar Vasiljevic preparation or in advance of trial type notes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, you say all these things were disclosed. Do you have anything to --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, and the electronic discovery system is a system set up to facilitate disclosure. I can find out when they were put in that system but it sounds like the system has worked. They were there for Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Find out for me and let me have that information. In the meantime we are going to commence the cross-examination with Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have a few more questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I thought you had finished. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, I haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You haven't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just with that one exhibit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Okay, very well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Turjacanin, I'm going to show you some still photographs and I'm going to ask you a series of questions about them. The first one I'd ask you to look at is 65 ter number 175.10.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you recognise what's depicted in 65 ter number 175.10?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is depicted?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Two houses. The house of Sadikovic and also the crime place and the house where is this garage door.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to make some marks on this photograph with the assistance of the usher. I'd ask you to begin by putting ZT on the bottom of the photograph to remind us that it is you who made these marks.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see your house in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle the old section of your house and put ZT1?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle the new portion of your house and put ZT2.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see the Sadikovic house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please circle that and put an S to indicate Nedzib Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see where the Meho Aljic house was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please circle that and put MA to indicate.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally I would ask you can you -- you mentioned seeing Milan Lukic at a neighbour's house where you were having coffee. Can you see that house in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to circle it and put the initials DK to indicate the initials of the person who were saying you had coffee with, Dzemila Kahriman?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Kahriman. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this photograph with its markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number P133.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this time, Your Honour, I would call up 65 ter number 175.11.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Turjacanin, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before you make any marks on this photograph, can I ask you to put your initials, ZT, at the bottom of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You are working with a blue pen, and I'd ask you once again to circle your house and put the initials ZT to indicate that's where your house is.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I have two, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, please put ZT1 to indicate the old house and ZT2 to indicate the new house.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is the location where the Meho Aljic house visible, where it was visible on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to circle where that is and place MA.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: All the house, all around the whole house?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the area where the house was.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Which house?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The house owned by Meho Aljic.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And please put MA inside that circle.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can I ask you now to draw a blue line indicating the path that you say you were taking from your house to the Meho Aljic house.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can I ask you just to put an arrow to indicate the direction you were walking.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, could I ask the usher to change the colour of the pen from blue to read. And I ask you now to -- you described fleeing after you escaped the house. Can I ask you to draw the path that you took when you fled the burning house using the red marker. It will be the same pen that you were using before. It's the same -- it's an electronic pen, Ms. Turjacanin. You can use the same pen. It will just appear red.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And please put an arrow to indicate the direction you were running.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I now ask that the witness be shown 65 ter number 175.12.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Turjacanin, it may take a minute or two for this photograph to appear before you. While it is being loaded into the computer, can I ask you where you went after you left the fire.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I went to the Megdan, which is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Unintelligible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer. The interpreter had difficulty hearing you.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I went to the Megdan, which has a Serb population, populated with a Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you go to specific houses?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not post that I wished to work with. It's 175.12, and the ERN number is 05449609.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe your physical condition shortly after the fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I remember everything which happened, but because of my burns to my face and to my hand I was feeling very ill.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We are now looking at 65 ter number 175.12. Can you see that on the screen before you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This is a still from the computer programme that you were describing for us earlier. Can I ask you to place the initials ZT-G on your garage.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to put -- the house on the left, who owned that house again, please?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Nedzib Sadikovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to put his initials on that house to indicate that's where he lived.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can we see in this photograph the house where you and the women were having coffee and -- before the fire that you've testified about?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you circle that and again put the initials of the woman you were having coffee with, Dzemila Kahriman.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is the -- the place where you first saw Milan Lukic the evening of the fire visible on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. At that house that's the first time I saw Milan Lukic at that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm now talking about the night of the fire. Your first observation of him the night of the fire, is that location visible on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've referred in your testimony to an uncle or cousin. Is the location where you first saw this person visible on the photograph that's before you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please mark that with a circle and perhaps simply put an X.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was Milan Lukic the first time you saw him in relation to the -- what we can see in this image?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
