utterances.text: You've made a dot in the middle of the path; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to put ML under that dot to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally could I ask you to draw a line to indicate the path that you took from your house towards the Meho Aljic house.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I now ask the witness -- sorry, may I tender that into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit number P136.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that now the witness be shown Exhibit 175.13.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Apologies to the counsel, it's Exhibit number P135.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While that photograph is being loaded into the system -- well, it seems it's now here before us. Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph, the 65 ter number 175.13?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before you make any marks, could you please put ZT on the bottom to indicate that it's your markings.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does this photograph depict the path that you and the other members of your family took to the Meho Aljic house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please draw a line to indicate that.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit number P136.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if we could then see 65 ter number 175.14.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While that's being called up, Ms. Turjacanin, where did you spend the night, the night after you escaped the fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Partly at the Megdan, and the second part of the night I returned to Bikavac.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you returned to Bikavac did you stay in a particular house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: When I went back to Bikavac I went back for a precise reason. That means to say I went specifically while there were still people of Bikavac, and I wanted to warn them to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you go to houses in the Bikavac area and warn people to leave?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many houses do you recall going to?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Four, four. On the fourth I stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was the name of the person in -- or the family in that house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The fourth house where I stayed the family was called Salic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before you on the screen you can see 65 ter number 175.14. Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The crime scene I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you see a portion of the house of Nedzib Sadikovic in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to first put your initials at the bottom of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can I ask you to put an NS on the portion of the house of Nedzib Sadikovic that we can see?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can I ask you to circle the location where the Meho Aljic was and put an MA into that.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender the photograph with these markings into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is admitted as Exhibit P137.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the final picture I'd like -- or ask you to look at is 65 ter number 175.15. While that's being called up, you've just -- I'm sorry, it looks like it's coming on the screen now. This is a picture of -- from the still video that you referred to earlier in your testimony. Can I ask you to circle where you believed you climbed out of that night.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I didn't really understand what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've testified that these doors were similar to the doors that were blocking the Meho Aljic house. If you're able, can I ask you to circle how it was you were able to get past these doors or the doors that looked like these doors.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And once again would you put your initials at the bottom of this photograph so that we know.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I would tender this into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's admitted as Exhibit P138.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you touch the doors as you climbed through them?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What do you remember about the doors as you climbed through -- through them?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: My -- my hands were burnt because the doors were burning. They were too hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you touch the doors with your hands?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the morning after the fire. Where did you go the morning after the fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I went to the command of the Serb army, Serbian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ask them to do something when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you ask them to do?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I asked them to shoot me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did anyone shoot you at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Again at the house of Salic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when someone came, a medical person came to the house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, a doctor came.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you know this doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was a medic who was tending to the staff of the place where I was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he bring you back to the hospital in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did he remain with you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What, if anything, did he do for you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: For me he didn't do anything. He gave me some ointment and/or cream and pills.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever come back to administer medical treatment to you again?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you remain in the Salic house?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Eleven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Why did you leave on the eleventh day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Because on the eleventh day a soldier of the army who was close to the house came to warn me that I should leave because Milan Lukic knew that I was there, and I was warned that he would come and try to finish me off.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The night of the fire, did you ask anyone to go back to your house that -- that day or that night?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I asked my neighbour to go back to my house to help to open up the space in which my brother and cousin had taken refuge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you eventually left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you go to a place called Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, leading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness went to several places on the way. I'm just trying to in an uncontroversial manner just expedite my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Apparently Mr. Alarid doesn't think it's non-controversial, so let the witness give the evidence as to where she went.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you ultimately arrive after leaving Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: First of all I went to Okruglo where I stayed four days. Then I continued on my way and a few days later I reached Medjedja.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you get there? What was the means of transport?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: On foot. We crossed the hills and the mountains on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you encounter any Serb positions on your way to Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. We always encountered Serb positions. That's why we didn't travel during the day but, rather, during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd again object to the leading nature of the entire questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I would allow that one, Mr. Alarid. But I caution you again, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'll do my best, but it's my view that I'm not leading the witness, but I will do my best to ask even more vague questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I guess my definition of a non-leading question is: "What happened next?"

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not limited to a single question in my examination, Your Honour. A leading question is one that suggests an answer to the witness. I'm not suggesting any answers to this witness .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned that one of the places you were at on the way to Medjedja is a place called Okruglo. Did you attempt to get medical treatment in Okruglo?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any doctors in Okruglo?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the doctor or doctors that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe what happened during -- or your interaction with this Muslim doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I was just in too much pain because of all my wounds, and someone asked him to -- to take care of me, but he refused. He said, "It's not worth it. She's really on death's door, and so I might as well keep the medication for the soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What was your reaction to being told this by the doctor?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I said, "No, you're wrong. I can't die. I want to live."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm drawing your attention now to Medjedja. When you arrived in Medjedja, did you see someone that you knew?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would ask whether the pseudonym sheet is before the witness. If not, I ask that it -- could the corrected version be put? Your Honour, if I could hand correct so that the correct pseudonym is on the sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who did you meet in Medjedja, or who did you see?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I saw the individual VG-32.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe your first meeting with him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, this man was the husband of my best friend. VG-32 did not recognise me. So VG-32 asked me, he said, "Zehra, is it you?" And I said, "Yes, it is indeed me."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe your physical condition at the time you arrived in Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I was in an extremely poor condition both physically and emotionally because of the wounds and the bandages, and my hands were so burnt. They were infected, and so they were oozing, and in fact people were scared when they saw me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you receive treatment in Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who primarily administered that treatment?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left Medjedja?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The four Croatian soldiers came from Bosnia and took me to the hospital in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you get from Medjedja to Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, as before, on foot. We crossed mountains and hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at the screen in front of you and I'm going to ask that the Sanction system be put on. After you escaped the fire did you give several statements about what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After you escaped the fire, did you give several statements to journalists and other people about what happened to you in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After arriving in The Hague, were you asked to look at some video recorded statements from around this time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I am not going to ask you to look at these videos again here, but I am going to ask you to confirm whether or not the image you see in front of you, which is from 65 ter number 168, is the beginning of one of the videos that you watched this week.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did it fairly and accurately depict the interview as best you can recall?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would tender this statement -- or this video recording, Prosecution Exhibit -- Prosecution 65 ter number 168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just for clarification, we've received two transcripts and then -- that were undated and one transcript of a tape that was dated, and so we'd like some clarification of if this is the dated one or one of the two non-dated ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't have all the information here, but what I can say is this: That one of the videotapes if you recall was introduced through VG-32. So -- and to save time I'm not even going to establish -- it's already in evidence. This one I have introduced, and the third one was not put on the 65 ter list but it was disclosed because it was a prior statement of -- of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you able to assist Mr. Alarid in identifying it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll ask Mr. Van Hooydonk to look up once the information from 65 ter number 168.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just for some help, Your Honour, one of the statements is five pages transcribed with a journalist noted as the interviewer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just a few questions of this witness. Can I complete my examination? I will assist their Mr. Alarid any way I can before his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alarid, let Mr. Groome finish.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 65 ter number 168 is admitted as Exhibit number P139.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Ms. Turjacanin, I'd ask you now at this point to look around the courtroom and tell us whether you recognise anyone here aside from myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The accused was not asked to stand. The accused who is standing will sit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that you do not recognise anyone here in the courtroom today?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to summarise your -- the injuries that you sustained, first your physical injuries?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I suffered from third-degree burns. I'm missing part of my ears, and my hands are completely paralysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you receive skin grafts to repair some of the damage to your skin?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And you said that your hands are paralysed. Are you able to function normally at present given the state of your hands?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is there any prospect that your hands will return to a normal condition?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Unfortunately, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What has been the psychological implications of what occurred to you in the course of this fire?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It's really too complex, too difficult to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If you could summarise. Do you now, 16 years after, still feel the effects of what happened to you that night?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My final question to you here today is can you describe for the Chamber the overall impact of what happened to you on Vidovdan night in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: All that happened on the 27th of June, 1992, all of the suffering, all of the pain that I was subjected to and that I will continue to be experiencing for the rest of my life, but despite all of that, I would say only one thing, I'm still alive and life is beautiful, and I still wish to live a full life.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I wonder if you could help me with something. I would want something in the transcript to be clarified. Page 20, line 9 of the transcript where the witness was saying that she went to visit her neighbour Sena Subasic and that a colleague of hers came to visit, and the name of that person is Milan Lukic. Is that the person -- another person, or is it the same person as the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I can clarify that with a couple of questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've testified earlier about a colleague of yours from work. Can I ask you to say his name and then also please spell his last name so it's clear the person you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I really want to have two things clarified about these names because they're similar. Milan Lukic and Milan Lucic are two different persons. Milan Lukic and Milan Lucic are two different people. Milan Lucic was my friend and colleague. He was a really good person. And Milan Lukic is the one who inflicted all the wounds and suffering that I have described to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to please spell the last name of your colleague just so that it is completely clear.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: L-u-c-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Does that clarify it? I have no questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: May I ask you, witness, French is not your native language. You may be naturally liguistically gifted. So I'd like to find out whether there is any particular reason why you're giving your evidence in French.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is. That's true. Everything I -- I lived through and experienced in Bosnia-Herzegovina, well, I've -- I've broke off all contacts with Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so I -- I've distanced myself from there. Today I have a new home country, and that's where my new life is, and that's why I want to use the language of that new country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Turjacanin. My name is Jason Alarid, and I represent Milan Lukic, and I have to ask you a few questions. Can we -- can we do that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I can tell as you sit here that you are traumatised, and I can tell as you sit here that you've experienced a lot of pain. I have a good friend who was burned over 90 per cent of his body and the recovery was horrendous, so I know that you've gone through a lot because I've seen your videos. I've seen your scars. I'll sorry for that. Now, in preparation for my -- this case, we were given several statements by you, some of them to the media or the news -- the television, and a couple that were written down. Do you remember giving statements to the television after you escaped from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Approximately how many times did you give statements to the television, let's say?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I don't remember. I don't remember. In fact, my answer would be no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So you're saying you did not give statements to television?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did make statements, but I don't know how many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Understood. Well, if we have three times and three transcripts related to television interviews, would that refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could it have been more?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, is it true that you also gave testimonials that were reduced to writing, to statement form?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you give interviews with investigators of war crimes?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How many times did you meet with the Office of the Prosecutor in this case at any time in your history?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you -- do you recall meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor in December of 2000, over two days at your home in France?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you were asked several questions about the incident just like you are today. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know if your statements were recorded?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was anything ever reduced to writing for you to look at and review?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, would you agree that a murder of this magnitude, 70 people in a home, is a very important crime?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: It's a crime that deserves investigation and pursuit by all available authorities. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you ever speak with Bosnian police investigators?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Were you ever interviewed by police officers that wanted to hear your story?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I no longer remember. I can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The reason I ask you this is many witnesses that have come to this court to testify have given both statements to the Prosecution of this court as well as officers of Bosnia, and I did not see interviews from you to either of them. Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I'm just wondering why a crime of such magnitude is not documented amongst police officers of your countries since you were recovering there.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that no -- nothing took place. I didn't say there was no communication with the police. I don't remember. I don't remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- which organisation that was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's hear Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just as a point clarity, the third video that was provided Mr. Alarid was given -- was a videotaped interview by an investigative Judge taken in 1993, and with respect to the document that was -- the Chamber asked me to get some information on, that was first disclosed in March of 2004, so over four years ago, and I redisclosed it as well without any redactions on the 22nd of September 2008. I believe the original one had the address redacted at that time. So it's been -- it was disclosed over four years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, for the record we did not get it and we're still looking in the batch of September 20th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But for the record it was disclosed. Now, I believe you ought to be moving to another point, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is probably the most important witness in this case. I will put to the witness that I don't necessarily believe this happened from the statements that occurred, the statements that I'm sure you'll get to read, and maybe from the testimony of this witness, and I have to get to the bottom of it, but I understand what the delay with the French translation and of course the delicate condition of this witness I must move slow and I apologise, but I would ask for the patience of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm naturally and normally a patient person, Mr. Alarid, but this particular point I thought you had exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. Could the court assistant please upload 1D10-2599 with the B/C/S version 1D10-2604, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'm asking you to look and read the start -- do you recognise your name at the top of this document? And I believe it says: "Zehra Turjacanin, the sole survivor of the inferno during the night of 27 June 1992 describes about everything she saw and heard from witnesses who survived the hideous crime in Visegrad municipality." Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to be clear it said the "hideous crimes," not the "hideous crime."

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise that, ma'am? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I actually need my glasses.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you have them with you? Can you put them on?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No, they're not here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll ask the usher to fetch her glasses so they can be used by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If I could ask you a few questions and you can tell me whether you disagree with that. At the top of this statement and in other televised statements you specifically state that you were one of the last remaining 753 Muslims who managed to escape from Visegrad, and you used the term 753 in other places in your statements, and I'm wondering why you're so precise on that number. Could you explain that, please?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, my first question was do you recognise that this would be a statement from you, things that only you would have known, things that you gave to an investigator or what-not that was reduced to writing?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, then let's go through some of the things that are documented here and see if you would agree that you would say that or not say that. Is that okay? Do you agree that -- do you agree that you were one of the last 753 Muslim who managed to escape from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And why do you use the number 753? Why are you so precise with that number?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Because when we stopped to rest during the day in the forest, the men who were leading the convoy, they counted how many we were quite accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: So that no one would be left behind in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: And that's why I know that it was that number 753, and it's precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, this is an exodus of your people from Visegrad that occurred how long after the fire, how long after St. Vitus Day?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but about 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how was it that this number of people, 753 people, were gathered into one area to make this exodus over the mountains and the valleys?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: When I arrived in Okruglo, the men returned from Visegrad to gather, to assemble all of the people who were still left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many -- and how many men were -- were facilitating this exodus? How many Bosnian soldiers were helping this group?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Specifically those were not soldiers. Those were just people who gathered to try and assemble all the population in order to avoid any further crimes and to save what could still be saved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many of these men were -- were leading this exodus?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I can't say for sure, but approximately 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how many people went with you to Okruglo?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I left with four men and one elderly lady to go to Okruglo.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And did the journey at least to there, were you only accompanied by these five other people?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how long did that journey take on foot?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly. Ten hours about.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, in the statement in front of you it says that, "My story could begin from the moment when the Uzice Corps arrived in Visegrad and began taking away Muslim men." Do you -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is it true --

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: -- that the Uzice Corps were taking away Muslim men when they arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how did that make your community and, more importantly, how did that make you feel during that time?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Awful.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was there a lot of talk in your community, in your neighbourhood amongst the Muslim people about this oppression that was coming to you?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What kind of things were discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The taking away of men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was escape or running away discussed?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Why did you not leave at this time? Why did you not escape Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: All those who tried to escape from Visegrad were stopped some place or another.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at this point in time you state that the Muslim men were kept as prisoners at the Vilina Vlas Hotel but there were no killings yet. How did you know the men were kept at the Vilina Vlas Hotel?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The information came from Serb men who were not terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you speak personally with any of these men?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And they also told you there was no killings yet?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: That, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was there fighting already going on between the Serbs and the Bosnian forces?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could you repeat yourself, ma'am? There was no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: In Visegrad there was never any fighting between the Serbs and the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, it's -- according to your statement, it's at this time "the crimes began sometime in April this year when townsman Milan Lukic came from Serbia after spending four years in Obrenovac." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And it further states that: "He came as a member of the White Eagles. He had his six White Eagles --"

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you know this? How did you know that Milan Lukic was back in town?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: All of the people in that town knew that Milan Lukic had returned to town. As soon as he returned, he started with his mischief.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so there was a lot of talk amongst your countrymen about a Milan Lukic. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when you first heard the name Milan Lukic, was your memory refreshed that you knew who this man was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long have you lived in Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: My whole life.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in the house that you identified for the Prosecutor and you marked as your home, how long had you lived in that home?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: My whole life I spent in my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so you -- that was the home where you spent your time as a small child, as a young girl, a young woman, never having moved or relocated?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So there was a time that you had moved from the house or you'd stayed there the whole time? Please clarify.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: We always lived in the same place, and -- and then at some point to our other house.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is that the house right next door?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when did you move from the old house into the new house? Can you remember the year?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: We never really moved. We just went from one house to the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you stated that you did not or you were not reminded that you knew who this Milan Lukic was. When were you first reminded that you knew who this Milan Lukic was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: When people started speaking about him. My brother started telling us that this was a schoolmate of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when did you remember smoking cigarettes with him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I never smoked with Milan Lukic or in his company, but we were together in the same group behind the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, that's -- to me that's sort of the same thing, even -- did you speak to him during these times?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did your brother speak with him during these times?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Was your brother friends with him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I believe you stated that they were in -- were they in the same classroom or just the same class together?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The same classroom, the same class. The same thing, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, how many students were there in the secondly school in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but there were more than a thousand students.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We are going to take the break now. The witness will leave the courtroom before we do. When she has left, I will give a decision of the Trial Chamber on a Prosecution motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I take this opportunity to give the Chamber's decision on the Prosecution motion which was filed on the 22nd of September for leave to add an updated statement and tables for the witness Amor Masovic, director of the state commission for tracing missing persons in Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the normal course of proceedings the Defence teams would have two weeks in which to respond to the motion, that is Monday, the 6th of October, but the Prosecution list of witnesses for the remainder of the case indicates that this witness will be called on Wednesday, the 1st of October. In the Chamber's view this is a case in which the practice of expedited response would not be appropriate for a variety of reasons. For one, it would deprive the Defence teams of the usual time to prepare their responses at a time when there is already a high level of motions in the Chamber. Fourteen motions have been filed in the past three weeks alone with more than 300 pages of attachments to review. The updated table and charts will require close comparison with those already disclosed, and tomorrow is the last sitting day before Masovic is scheduled to be heard. In the circumstances, the Chamber rules that Amor Masovic is not to be called until after the Defence teams have had time to respond in the normal way and the Chamber has determined the motion. We are adjourned for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness is being brought in, I presume. Mr. Alarid, are you in a position to tell us how much time you will need?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I could -- the problem is -- and I think it's just from a practical perspective, the responses and delays between the answers are so slow and necessary of course by the addition of the French translation. That's why I can't really give an honest estimate. If we were going question and answer in rapid succession I could probably be a little more precise but that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At some time during the proceedings during the session we'll have to address some practical issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe the witness may not -- if it's the French that's slowing us down, I think if that were explained to the witness she may very well be willing to speak in her native tongue, B/C/S, if the Chamber thought that would speed it up. I would ask the Chamber to consider addressing that with her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I'd want to ask, because she's already explained why she wants to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could maybe add one piece of information to that. She did inform me during the course of proofing that if she were questioned by someone who spoke her native tongue, she would then be responding to that person in her native tongue because she felt she could be more precise, so that's why I suggested it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, may I ask you something? You are testifying in French, and our experience is that it takes a little longer with the translation and therefore with the entire proceedings. Would you be prepared to testify in your native tongue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid then.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Ma'am, when we went on the lunch break we were talking about how you and your brother originally knew Milan Lukic. You indicated that you were four years older than Milan, at least in school?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you -- but you also indicated that your brother was in the same homeroom as Milan?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, what do you mean four years older than Milan in school?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: She was four years ahead of him, I guess, but of course someone could be a different age and still be four years ahead in school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So, Witness, is that what you meant, you were four years ahead of Milan in school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was three years ahead of Milan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just to clarify that, ma'am, what's the year of your birth? Just the year.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: 3rd December, 1962.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so if -- in your statement you indicate that Milan Lukic was born in 1968, and so I just -- that's why I asked you the question, because that's a six-year differential in your ages, but yet you're three years apart in school.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I never said that Milan Lukic's age. I said -- I said -- in 1968. In 1968. I'm sorry I never said Milan Lukic's year of birth was 1968. I said my brother's year of birth was 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And that is -- but because your brother's year of birth is 1968, you indicate in your statement in front of you that that is why you know Milan was born in 1968. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: My brother was born in 1968, and he went to school -- he started going to school one year earlier than envisaged by the law in Bosnia and Herzegovina, whereas I, during my schooling, lost one year. So that made the difference between us five years. Now, as for Milan Lukic, I don't know exactly what year he was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, I'm just going off what's in your statement in front of you. So that's why I'm asking you to clarify. And isn't it true that you ended that paragraph, that first paragraph, with that you hope that it will show that Milan Lukic is the criminal most responsible for destruction of human lives in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's a blatant misquote of what's there. It's "If the truth about what happened at Visegrad comes out one day, and I hope it does." That's the context that "hope" was used in, not that she hopes that Milan Lukic is going to be implicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's very correct, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I was trying to redact, but I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, you can't redact in that way without putting the whole thing in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: So just taking the full sentence into context, ma'am: "If the truth about what happens -- or happened in Visegrad comes out one day, and I hope it does, it will show that Milan Lukic is the criminal most responsible for the destruction of human lives in Visegrad." You said that in your statement at the beginning, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: And I confirm that now here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Are you stating through your testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Now, this minute, I confirm that if any investigation is carried out it will be established that Milan Lukic is the worst criminal in Visegrad who destroyed men, women, and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, you go on in your statement to state that: "According to the records about the Territorial Defence, it is certain that 6.600 members, inhabitants, excuse me, of Visegrad were either taken to camps or killed." Where did you get that information, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you indicated that there were three camps, the Prelovo village camp, the Vilina Vlas, and another one in Zamnica. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I confirm that, yes. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how did you confirm that, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Based on the testimony of persons who escaped these camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just in terms of -- I believe this paragraph is talking the Territorial Defence in and of itself and stating that: "They took possession of their cars, gold, money, foreign currency, and technical appliances and took them away and killed them." Who are you meaning by "they"?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Milan and the group that he organised. Milan who organised that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And is this again the group of six members?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, is one of those -- you indicate in your statement that one of these six members was a woman?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: The seventh person was a woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And she killed men by cutting off their genitals and then they drained the blood from them and sent it to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you hear about that, or did you witness that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But it was in your statement, and can you read it there from before?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Maybe. It's been many years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you indicate that they, again -- every time you refer to "they" are you referring to Milan Lukic and these six or seven other people?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I mean Milan Lukic and the group that he organised and the Serb locals of Visegrad who assisted him in destroying people in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This document that's still being -- that's continually being referred to as a statement, could I ask Mr. Alarid to please establish with the witness that it is her statement by showing her a signature page or something else. It's my information that it's actually an excerpt from a book written by someone else that includes an account of what she has said, and I'm not sure how much is hers and how much is the author of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I guess the point of contention is noted. However, the Court just introduced a newspaper article that was written in both first and third person supposedly that was a statement of my client but this entire thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Let us see the source of the document, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We do not have the source. It was tendered by the Prosecution. This came in their batch. We have no way of verifying this since it came in their disclosures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What do you mean tendered by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Meaning it was disclosed to us. It was part of their disclosure batches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But tendered is the wrong word.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It was disclosed to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes. That's the only reason I have it and it's written in the first person so that's why I assume it's a statement. When someone said, "I, I, I," over again it seems to be logical that it was the statement of the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It's just a dangerous assumption to make when there's no signature on the page itself, Your Honour, or any of the pages as far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, what is the principal purpose of -- behind your use of this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: To -- well, first and foremost to state if she had said this or believed it or believed it to be true. I believe there are -- if you put it into play with the other video excerpts which are the lion's shares of our other statements, if you will, I think they are somewhat consistent all the way across the board with what she states, although there's some minor discrepancies between each but that would be natural in terms of an interview situation. But I think it is very probative, because it shows the witness's state of mind, perception, and an ideation of what the war was at the time and an ideation of who Milan Lukic was and what he was at the time, including giving a detailed account or as detailed maybe as was here in court today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But in the absence of anything from you as to its source --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- and its authenticity, what weight are we to attach to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I would agree in the loose confines of admissibility in the courts I think that it's up to you to give it the proper weight, of course, at the end but it would not affect the admissibility of a document, especially considering we got it from the Prosecution. I mean it's not like I'm coming to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please stop saying you got it from the Prosecution. The Prosecutor disclosed it to you. When the Prosecutor discloses a document he does not make any admission as to its admissibility. He's obliged to disclose it. He's not saying it's admissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I would agree with that, Your Honour, but we have no other way of doing due diligence. If you look at the history of this case this was a delayed disclosure case and so we didn't get any of the material in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't want a mystery from you. We've heard that history before so I don't want that. Now I'd like you to conclude your examination on the basis of this document as quickly as possible and move on to another subject. You are right. It will be for the Trial Chamber to attach what weight we wish to the document and to the witness's response to your questions on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, and, Your Honour, you will be able to see for yourself and I guess it was really just how it fell into my -- into my binder here, but I think there's a lot of consistencies in the story between the interview transcripts as well as this, so I mean as we make our final submissions there will be a detailed compare and contrast between the statements done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, did you believe at that there were people being executed underneath the hotel in a pipe where they were gassing people? Or suffocating, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. I think they did that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And was this something you observed or something you heard?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I heard that, and I cannot confirm it with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And of course you heard that they were bringing girls as young as 12 and 14 to the hotel for their whims and needs, and you heard that as well?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you had heard that there were some survivors of this tragedy; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but you did disclose in all your statements, of course, that VG-32 had helped you and assisted you and you'd spoken with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And of course VG-32 -- and VG-32 had disclosed to you that he had survived a firing squad. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you see the paragraph mentioning VG-32's name? Is it in front of you or do we have to go one more page? I think we might have to go one more page. It would either be at the very bottom or the top of the next page. And maybe the court assistant could go because I do not see his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant please go to the second page of the B/C/S version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you see there at the second paragraph, did you see VG-32's name?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And just looking at that, I notice that there is no mention of -- of Milan Lukic as being one of the offenders in that firing squad. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In that paragraph there's no mention of Milan Lukic as being one of the executors or potential executors of VG-32. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: VG-32 confirmed it with us himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And -- but again, though, this was hearsay information that you received well after you'd escaped from Visegrad. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. VG-32 himself told me about the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I would like to back up a little bit and talk about Milan Lukic. Can you describe him, the last time you saw him before the war?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He was a tall man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How tall?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. A young man.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How young was he the last time you saw him, if you can tell us.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I can't be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can you describe his hair, its colour?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Brown.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did -- as a younger man how did he wear his hair?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Like all men. Nothing specific, nothing particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, did he wear it short, long, or medium?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was a normal hair length, standard length for men.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If you could just describe what standard length for men is in your words. If you can, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I would like to try and explain in precise way. I want to find the right words to describe it. Can I show you on my own head?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: As long as you describe it as you do, ma'am, so the record can pick up your words.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: This length, standard length, and there was nothing special, nothing peculiar that would attract my attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember his eye colour, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you remember any identifying features of his face, anything peculiar that would remind you that it's Milan?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: As a younger man did he wear any facial hair?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember. Last time I saw him -- the last time I saw him he did not have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And are you talking about 1992 or before when he was in school, because I'm talking about when he was younger, when he was in school.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. When he was going to school he did not have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what about in 1992? Can you describe him?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Similarly, I can tell you he was a young man, tall. His hair was always dark brown.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did he wear it?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I cannot understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How -- what style was his hair cut?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, your brother, what school did he graduate from? Did he graduate from a specific school or class?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: He completed school for welders.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you remember in what year, ma'am, he graduated?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, what was he wearing in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Once I saw him in black clothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And a coat, I believe?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: And after that, later -- yes, he had a coat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Later I saw him in a regular military uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the colour of the military uniform? What was the style?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It was brownish with green -- green insignia, green markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Anything -- any hats?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to go back to the history --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to go back to the history a little bit, and in the statement that I saw it said: "After the White Eagles committed their crimes and left, Milan Lukic and his six White Eagles from Obrenovac remained in Visegrad, and he joined the so-called Serbian Territorial Defence who were in fact local Chetniks, and he continued to commit these crimes." First I'd like to ask you is this, is how did you know that White Eagles had left? What gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I can't answer precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, when the next -- the next bit of information is that: "Milan Lukic and his White Eagles from Obrenovac remained." How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember that time, that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you know he joined the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I never said he joined the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you believe that from some source?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, on direct examination, and I believe in your statement you indicated that you had a view of the new bridge of Visegrad from your home in Bikavac. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How far away is your house from the new bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Two kilometres, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in your statement and in later video interviews, you indicated that you knew that: "147 men were killed at the new bridge the night after the first day of the Kurban Bajram. The Chetniks brought them, threw them off the bridge and shot them as they were falling into the water. I watched this with my own eyes." Do you believe that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I believe that, and I saw the Chetniks killing those men on Bajram day. I cannot be sure only that there were exactly 147.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how are you sure that there was exactly 147?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: She just testified she was not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I cannot be sure only that there were exactly 147. I'll ask her to clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you know if there was 147?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I just said I couldn't answer that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you do --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, could court assistant bring up 1D20-0016, please. That's I believe incorrect. It's 1D20-0016. So it's 20 instead of 1D10.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, unfortunately nothing comes up in the system under 1D20-0016.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We uploaded it, Your Honour, but I do have a single copy we could use for the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, this is -- what's being placed next to you on -- on the ELMO, and you probably can see it on your television screen, is a photograph I received from the Office of the Prosecutor, and it has several Xs or crosses marking places in and around Visegrad. There is a cross at Bikavac. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And there is another cross to the left of that for the old bridge, the Stari Most bridge.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And then at the top of the page there is a bridge across the Drina that's not marked with a cross. Is that the new bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it's this distance between the -- let's say the X in Bikavac and the new bridge that is approximately two kilometres. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that it's very difficult to see something that's two kilometres away even from a balcony?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I have to be precise when answering this question. The new bridge that I see from my balcony is much closer as the crow flies than two kilometres, and for that reason at that short distance between the house and the bridge we have a much better view than if you took the road towards the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a good aerial view of Visegrad and showing that old bridge, the new bridge, and Bikavac?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, regardless, I would tender the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Alarid and the parties in general, I believe we now have to make an assessment as to the situation relating to this witness's testimony. Are you in a better position now to indicate the time that you have? In any event, I'll ask the court deputy to let me know how much time you have used. The Prosecutor used two hours and a 11 minutes. How much time -- how much more time would you be using?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, I will definitely exhaust my allotted time, Your Honour, but I would like a little consideration considering the pace of the Prosecution's testimony was a little bit quicker. Maybe that was because of the, you know, some of the facts being injected in the questions, but I just feel pressed only because there's longer pauses on the record between my questions and the answers, and so I -- that's why I have such a hard time telling you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, how much time would you be using?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is very difficult for me to say. Maybe 15 minutes, maybe half an hour, maybe 40 minutes, but I will try to make all examination as short as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, it's clear that we will not finish with this witness's testimony by 1.45. May have a word with the legal officer, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we have been considering various options as to the best way in which to conclude this witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, we have been considering the best way in which to conclude this witness's testimony, and I'd like her to know that we have regard to the condition that she's in, that she's a person who has been severely traumatised, but we have tried our very best to see whether there was any way of continuing this afternoon and concluding her testimony, but it is simply not possible having regard to all the circumstances, including not least of all the obligation to be fair to the Defence. It looks, therefore, that the witness will have to return, regrettably, next week, and if it is next week, it will have to be on Thursday, because on Wednesday we already have, I believe, a video-conference -- a video-conference link schedule. Having said that, please continue, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. Could we admit the photo, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Could the court assistant see if another photo will call up hopefully 1D20-0022.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the previous document, 1D20-0016 becomes Exhibit number 1D54.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you see --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And could we get slightly smaller, please, I believe?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you recognise that this photo is of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you see the Bikavac neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would the court assistant please give the witness a marking device for the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Would you mind at the bottom left-hand corner where there's no houses or anything to please sign the photo, please, or the screen. ZT is fine.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, ma'am, could you please put a circle, a small circle where your home is in Bikavac, please.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but this is a relatively small-scale image and I'm unable to locate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: But you can see the new bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Put a small X on that, please.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if I were to just point your attention to the Bikavac neighbourhood, which is middle right at the very bottom of the page, would that help orient you to the photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I have to know exactly what I'm doing, yet I can't really pinpoint it in this image.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: That's fine, ma'am. Now, from where your balcony is, though, you testified on direct examination that you could hear the bodies in the water from the distance of your home to the new bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Doesn't it seem like that would be extremely difficult considering it's two kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: It is not that difficult. It's very easy to see everything that goes on from my balcony, what goes on at the new bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, you indicated that this was at night and that you saw vehicles with their headlights on and then turned them off on the bridge. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it might be okay to see headlights at two kilometres away, but I put to you that it would be very difficult to hear something hitting the water at two kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I can only confirm that you can hear the sound. When a body drops into the water, you can hear the echo of the body splashing against the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'd like to admit this photograph, Your Honour, as marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, becomes Exhibit 1D55.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can you tell me what date the first day of the Kurban Bajram was in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you tell me what day of the week it was?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How did you know it was the first day of the Kurban Bajram?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: Because this was a Muslim holiday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How long was it before June 26th?

utterances.speaker: ZEHRA TURJACANIN
utterances.text: I -- I can't remember any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
